title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow?

options.text: Agent: the model's output decides which steps the system runs next
Workflow: the model picks a label, but every path was written in code
Agent: the system branches, so it adapts to each request it gets
Workflow: it calls the model once, and agents always call it several times

items.stem:
Here is the core of an assistant:

messages = [question]
for step in range(6):
    reply = model(messages, tools)
    if reply.tool_call is None:
        break
    messages.append(run_tool(reply.tool_call))

In one run the model requests check_calendar for Friday, then check_calendar for Saturday, then writes its answer. Who decided what in this run?

options.text: The code decided both calendar checks, because it executes run_tool each time
The model chose the checks, but the code chose when to stop, via the break
The model chose both checks and when to stop; the code only set the 6-step limit
The model chose Friday's check; the code chose Saturday's after seeing the result

items.stem: Students phrase booking requests in dozens of ways ("grab me the laser Thursday", "any slot on the cutter?"), but handling has always been the same three steps in one order: training record, calendar, book. A skipped training check once let an untrained student book. The model budget is small. Which design is best for this path?

options.text: A model call turns the message into fields; code then runs the three steps in order
An agent with the three tools, since varied phrasing needs the model to pick the steps
An agent with the three tools and a system prompt that lists the required order
Code runs the training check, then an agent handles the calendar and the booking

items.stem: Every model call costs $0.01. A fixed workflow always makes 3 model calls per request. An agent version makes between 2 and 8 model calls per request, and its loop has a hard cap of 8. Over 500 requests, how much more can the agent cost than the workflow in the worst case, in US dollars?

In the manual-search part of the assistant, a model call chooses each next page lookup and when to stop, and the program cuts it off at 6 lookups. Every lookup costs the same. Which statement about the cost of one question is right?

options.text: It is always 6 lookups' worth, because the loop runs until it reaches the cap
It has no upper limit, because a loop driven by a model cannot be capped
It is the same for every question, because the code decides how many lookups run
It varies from 1 to 6 lookups' worth by question; the cap bounds the worst case

items.stem: Three requests reach the assistant. A: "Book the laser cutter tomorrow at 3 pm, and tell me what training it needs." B: "Book me whichever printer can fit a 300 mm part this Friday." C: "What are the PLA fan settings on the Prusa, and is it free on Friday?" Only one is poorly served by a fixed workflow. Which one? Answer with the letter.
